MMG-N11.free_elimination: Week-3 profit is 1 3/4 times the combined loss, i.e. larger than the loss, so the total must be positive: both negatives struck without computing.
MMG-N11.error_directions: 690: forgets week 2 in the total (1050-360), above, not predictable; -180: profit computed on week-2 loss only (420-600), below; -1650: week-3 treated as a loss (-600-1050), below. Sign reasoning predicts both negatives are wrong.
MMG-N11.interior_parity: -180 and 450: different sign; key is the only positive besides 690
MMG-N11.grade_note: Multi-step signed rational arithmetic with mixed-number factor; 7.NS.3, stronger students.
MMG-N11.note: W2=-240, loss 600, W3=+1050, total 450. The positive-sign argument leaves a 2-way 450/690 choice.

MMG-D01.free_elimination: 120 is far too large for 6 bags of just over 1 pound (it is the ounce total).
MMG-D01.error_directions: 120: answer in ounces (6x20), above, predictable as wrong unit; 8.4: reads 1 lb 4 oz as 1.4, above; 7.8: reads as 1.3 or partial conversion, above. A student cannot easily predict the decimal-misreading side.
MMG-D01.extreme_single_bound: each bag > 1 lb so total > 6 (kills nothing)
MMG-D01.interior_parity: 7.8 and 8.4 both one-decimal near-misses; key 7.5 is the cleanest (6 x 1.25)
MMG-D01.grade_note: 5.MD.1 customary conversion with a mixed unit; most grade-5 students handle 4 oz = 1/4 lb.
MMG-D01.note: 1 lb 4 oz = 1.25 lb; x6 = 7.5. Key is smallest of the plausible three.

MMG-G10.error_directions: 16.71: arc from radius 3 (or half of arc) 12+4.71, below, not predictable; 28.26: quarter-circle area, above; 30.84: half-circle arc 12+18.84, above.
MMG-G10.extreme_single_bound: 12 + chord 8.49 < P < 12 + 12 = 24 (triangle inequality) brackets only the key, but is not cheaper than computing the arc
MMG-G10.interior_parity: 16.71 and 21.42 vs 28.26: all two-decimal pi products; no tell

MMG-O10.free_elimination: Interest is $80/yr, so $200 needs more than 2 years = 24 months: 4.8 struck (also non-whole months).
MMG-O10.error_directions: 4.8: works in wrong units/ratio (e.g. 0.4 x 12), below; 25: 2000/80 years-to-$2000 confusion or 200/8, below; 29: arbitrary near-miss, below. Key is largest; direction of errors not predictable from stem.
MMG-O10.interior_parity: 25 and 29: both whole, key 30 cleaner (2.5 years); 29 is an odd unexplained value
MMG-O10.arith_tell: 30 is the only option that is a whole number of half-years (2.5 yr) - a month count tied to a yearly rate
MMG-O10.grade_note: 7.RP.3 simple interest with a years-to-months conversion; the conversion step makes it high tier.
MMG-O10.note: I=2000*.04*t=200 -> t=2.5 yr = 30 months. Plug-back ascending (4.8,25,29,30) takes 4.

MMG-O09.free_elimination: A 12-minute miss on a 1-hour walk cannot be a 125% error.
MMG-O09.error_directions: 25: divides by the guess 48 instead of actual 60, above, predictable only if the student knows the two denominators; 125: 60/48 as percent, above; 52: arbitrary/48+... near nothing, above.
MMG-O09.interior_parity: 25 and 52: key 20 and 25 differ only by the denominator choice
MMG-O09.grade_note: 7.RP.3 percent error with a minute/hour conversion; typical mid.
MMG-O09.note: |48-60|/60 = 20%. Key smallest; the 20/25 pair is the real decision.

MMG-O05.error_directions: 15: 4*0.5 (no squaring) +13, above; 17: (4*0.5)^2+13, above; 23: squares to 2.5 or similar mis-step, above. Every natural error forgets that squaring 0.5 shrinks it, so all go above - predictable to a student who knows s^2 < s for s < 1.
MMG-O05.interior_parity: 15 and 17: both whole; key 14 = 13 + 1 is the smallest
MMG-O05.grade_note: 6.EE.2c evaluating a formula with an exponent and a decimal; the 0.5^2 trap is the content.
MMG-O05.note: 4*(0.25)+13 = 14. Key is the smallest option; bound s^2<s gives C<15 which kills all three but is essentially the work.

MMG-N14.error_directions: -14: leaves 0.2 x 10^-14 unnormalised, above; -12: stops at grams (one conversion missed), above; -3: only converts units, ignores the division exponent, above. Each omission inflates n; a student who knows converting to a larger unit and normalising both push n down can predict the most negative.
MMG-N14.grade_note: 8.EE.4 operations in scientific notation plus two unit conversions and renormalisation; high tier.
MMG-N14.note: 0.14 mg / 7e7 = 2e-9 mg = 2e-12 g = 2e-15 kg. Key is the extreme option.

MMG-N06.free_elimination: 2 packs = one of each = 12 plates vs 8 cups, unequal; struck by inspection.
MMG-N06.error_directions: 2: one pack each, below; 20: 12+8, above; 24: the LCM (item count, not packs), above.
MMG-N06.interior_parity: 5 and 20: key is the small whole count
MMG-N06.grade_note: 6.NS.4 LCM word problem with a final pack-count step; typical mid.
MMG-N06.note: LCM 24 -> 2 + 3 = 5 packs. Plug-back ascending: 2 fails, 5 works (2 tries).

MMG-O01.error_directions: 26: adds 6 instead of 24 then halves, below; 47: halves only the original 46 then adds 24, above; 58: halves the 24 only (46+12), above.
MMG-O01.grade_note: Multi-step whole-number word problem; grade-4 content, acceptable as a grade-5 low item.

MMG-D12.free_elimination: Slope is positive, so any year after 2016 must exceed 12.4: 10.7 struck.

MMG-G14.error_directions: 14.4: forgets the 1/3 for the cone, above; 7.2: radius/diameter or 36*10/50 slip, above; 4: rounding/using 1/3 with r 5.5 or 120/30, below.

MMG-N07.error_directions: 8: omits 0 or one endpoint, below; 5: counts only positives 1-5, below; 2: ignores the absolute value (integers between -5.6 and -3.6), below. Errors are undercounts, but a student cannot read that from the stem.
MMG-N07.grade_note: 6.NS.7 absolute value and ordering with mixed numbers, counting integers including zero; high tier.

MMG-O13.free_elimination: Mix price 4 is closer to 5 than to 2, so more than half (30) of the 60 lb is sunflower: 24 and 30 struck by a weighted-average argument.

MMG-O13.grade_note: 8.EE.8 mixture problem by a linear equation/system; typical mid.
MMG-O13.note: 2(60-s)+5s = 240 -> s = 40. Plug-back ascending 24,30,40: 3 tries. After the weighted-average strike, a 40/48 coin flip.

MMG-O04.free_elimination: Price is under $1 per foot, so feet must exceed 26: 20.8 struck.
MMG-O04.error_directions: 20.8: multiplies 26 x 0.80, below (struck); 31.2: division slip, below; 32.4: near-miss division, below. Key is largest; near-miss distractors not predictable.

MMG-O12.free_elimination: Water drains, so 10 min in it was deeper than the 17 in at 50 min: 12.2 struck.

MMG-O12.grade_note: Linear rate of change working backwards; grade 7/8 proportional reasoning, easy for grade 8.

MMG-G06.error_directions: 189: square + only two triangles, below; 216: four triangles only, below; 252: triangles + a 6x6 square or other slip, below. Errors are omissions so fall below; a test-wise student picks the largest for a 'total' surface area.

MMG-G06.note: 81 + 4(54) = 297. Key largest; every distractor is a partial sum (omission), so 'take the biggest' works.

MMG-D11.error_directions: 0.4: inverts the ratio (MAD / difference), below; 0.5: miscomputed ratio, below; 6: reports the difference of means, above.

MMG-D06.error_directions: -7.5: treats 12 as -12 (-45/6), below; -6.5: other sign slip, below; -4.2: divides by 5 (drops the 0 day), below. Errors all more negative; not predictable from the stem.
MMG-D06.grade_note: Mean is grade 6, but summing mixed-sign integers is 7.NS.1; for grade-6 mid this is above-typical.

MMG-N15.error_directions: -0.7: computes y - x magnitude with sign (|x|-|y|), above; -0.73: mixed slip, above; -1.36: e.g. -0.06 - 1.3 (cube-root error), above. Since x < 0 < y, x - y has magnitude |x|+|y|, the most negative combination; magnitude-subtraction errors are predictably above.
MMG-N15.interior_parity: -0.73 and -0.7: near-identical pair; key is the clean -1.9
MMG-N15.grade_note: 8.EE.2 cube and square roots of decimals, then signed subtraction; high tier.
MMG-N15.note: x = -0.6, y = 1.3; x - y = -1.9. Key smallest.

MMG-N04.error_directions: 45: the empty land (3/8 of 120), below; 30: 5/8 of the corn land, below; 57: 5/8 of 168 minus corn, below. Not predictable.
